key_themes: China chipmaking breakthrough (DUV lithography + ChangXin Memory IPO) hammers semiconductor stocks
Big Tech capex anxiety drags Nasdaq as Intel and Alphabet both sell off despite earnings beats
AI software outperforms hardware: ServiceNow surges on strong Q2 beat and agentic AI monetization

stocks.reason: Down ~4-5%: China state-backed firm began mass-producing DUV lithography tools; also circular-financing concerns around $250B OpenAI data-center backstop deal; Apple overtook Nvidia as world's largest company by market cap

Down ~12%: ChangXin Memory Technologies completed blockbuster $8.6B Shanghai IPO, stock surged 466% on debut, renewing fears of Chinese competition crushing NAND memory pricing; stock now 45% off June peak

Down ~6-7%: Bloomberg report that China's state-backed Naura Technology began mass-producing domestic immersion DUV chipmaking machines, threatening ASML's competitive moat in older-generation tool sales to China
Down ~7%: Broad semiconductor selloff triggered by China's DUV chipmaking breakthrough; contagion from ASML and Nvidia declines hit the entire chip sector
Down ~5%: ChangXin Memory Technologies' massive Shanghai IPO reinforced fears of Chinese competition in DRAM/NAND; memory sector broadly sold off alongside SanDisk

Down ~7.9% despite massive Q2 beat: EPS $0.42 vs ~$0.21 est., revenue $16.1B (+25% YoY, fastest growth in 15 years), AI/Data Center revenue +59%; investors punished stock over capex raise to $20B+ for 2026 and ongoing foundry losses

Up ~7%: Q2 beat on nearly every metric — EPS $0.90 vs $0.86 est., revenue $3.99B vs $3.93B est., subscription revenue +24.5% YoY; 50% of net new business is now non-seat-based, directly addressing agentic AI cannibalisation fears
Reported Q2 after close: EPS $2.41 vs $2.29 est. (+$0.12 beat); stock rose ~$15.78 to $321.06 on 2x average volume; raised FY2026 and Q3 guidance; AI infrastructure demand driving strong results

KeyBanc downgraded to Underweight (rare bearish rating) with $250 PT, citing weak iPhone demand, slowing upgrade cycles, higher prices reducing trade-ins, and June spending down 2% vs 3-year avg of +9%; also surpassed Nvidia as world's most valuable company

Upgraded to Buy at Phillip Securities (PT $425); last week earnings beat with Cloud revenue +82% YoY to $24.8B; but raised 2026 capex guidance to $195-205B, stoking investor worry; stock trading off post-earnings capex scare
Piper Sandler upgraded to Overweight, raised PT to $20 from $18; upgrade cites de-risked balance sheet, smooth R2 ramp, improved demand outlook; earnings due July 30
Jefferies upgraded to Buy from Hold, raised PT to $17.50 from $14.50, implying ~22% upside; EV strategy and cost-cutting progress cited as catalysts
HSBC downgraded to Reduce from Hold with PT cut to $191 from $231; concerns about slowing enterprise software demand and AI integration costs weighing on margins
Seaport Research downgraded to Neutral from Buy (no PT); also news that Paramount-Skydance put their WBD acquisition discussions on hold, removing a potential buyout premium
Wells Fargo upgraded to Equal Weight from Underweight, raised PT to $30 from $18 (+67% PT increase); shift signals improving subscriber retention and cost structure post-restructuring
